terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation; aliquem aliquid rogāre, the person and the thing both in the accusative
evidence: Plaut. Most. 5.1.70: aliud tē rogō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Classically the thing asked stands in the accusative beside the person only when it is a neuter pronoun or adjective (hoc tē rogō); otherwise rogāre aliquem dē aliquā rē (Lewis & Short). Quaerere ā (ex, dē) aliquō is to ask someone, enquire of him.

sources: Lewis & Short: rogo · Lewis & Short: quaero
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 93, checked against the searchable text and the page images of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
